evidence.note: Immediately separated the two deliverables, recognized y2kr-SC could reuse the reference alignment vs DM-HS needing topology alignment, and laid out an ordered two-part plan (parse data → strategy per pair).

Built a scorer that decomposes S3 into Ea/E2_aligned and derived concrete numeric sub-targets (e.g. 'need E2a<=15115', 'need Ea>=10229 or E2a<=11970') — milestones marked with the exact numeric bar to clear.

Repeatedly and deliberately sequenced which deliverable to work on based on intermediate scores ('run y2kr-SC first since it's closer to target'; 'DM-HS needs more improvement'), showing score-driven re-prioritization of the two targets.

Instead of factoring a shared parser/scorer/generic-aligner module, the agent wrote ~20 overlapping standalone scripts (v2/v3/v4/netal/greedy/greedy2/greedy3/icm/fast/sa/perturb...) with duplicated infrastructure — the optimizer stage was decomposed reactively rather than as planned checkpoints with re-seed gates.

Perturbation-trial loop functions as an implicit re-seed checkpoint mechanism toward the 0.55 bar, but was introduced ad-hoc rather than pre-planned; every milestone continued to be stated against its numeric threshold.

reasoning: The agent clearly cleared anchor 5 — distinct parse/score/align/optimize/write stages with the two thresholds treated as explicit per-deliverable milestones — and reached partway into anchor 8 via consistently numeric milestone bars and deliberate, score-driven sequencing of the easier DM-HS vs harder y2kr-SC targets, with a touch of anchor-10 adaptation (deriving intermediate Ea/E2a checkpoints and re-prioritizing deliverables). It falls short of a full 8 because it never factored the shared infrastructure (parser/scorer/generic aligner) from per-instance tuning, instead producing many duplicated ad-hoc scripts and decomposing the optimizer reactively rather than through planned checkpoints. This places it at a 6.
